entities.summary:
Gabriel de Gramont (1486–1534) was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal.

Born in unknown circumstances, de Gramont rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming Bishop of Béziers in 1519 and Cardinal-Priest of San Pietro in 1527.

De Gramont played a key role in the French Reformation, serving as a mediator between the Catholic and Protestant factions.

He was a prominent figure at the Council of Trent, where he advocated for reform and the implementation of the Tridentine Mass.

De Gramont's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped shape the course of the French Reformation and the development of Catholic doctrine.

This chapter in his life was marked by the tragic fate of his son, which he later wrote about in his letters, a stark reminder of the human cost of the Reformation.
